# Asañciccakathā (Kv 20.1)

**ID:** Kv 20.1
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Asañciccakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul27.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asañciccakathā* ("Discussion on the Unintentional") is the first discourse of the twentieth chapter (*pannāsa*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Devdas 2004]. The debate concerns whether committing one of the cardinal crimes (*ānantariya*) unintentionally (*asañcicca*)—such as killing one's mother, father, or an arahant, or causing a schism in the order—makes a person an *ānantarika*, that is, liable to immediate retributive retribution after death [Dube 1980; Devdas 2004]. The Theravādins defend the primacy of volition and intentional impulse in determining moral culpability, arguing that accidental or unintentional commission does not incur immediate retribution, whereas the opposing view, attributed by the tradition to the Uttarāpathakas, maintains that the heinous acts entail retribution regardless of whether they were intentional [Dube 1980; Bareau 1955; Devdas 2004].
